sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 85, recorded on June 24, 2022.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到 ADSP 播客第 85 期，录制于 2022 年 6 月 24 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host, Bryce, we continue part two of our four-part interview with Tony Van Eerd.
sentences.zh: 我是康纳，今天我的联合主持人是布莱斯，我们将继续与托尼·范·埃德进行四部分访谈的第二部分。

sentences.en: Here's another story I just told the other day at work.
sentences.zh: 这是我前几天在工作时刚讲的另一个故事。

sentences.en: You would get bugs, right?
sentences.zh: 你会遇到Bug，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, like I'm working on BlackBerry.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像我在黑莓工作时。

sentences.en: We'd get a bug report that, you know, someone's typing and scrolling and there's the trackpad
sentences.zh: 我们会收到一个Bug报告，你知道的，有人在打字和滚动，然后那个触控板

sentences.en: and it got confused about whether you were touching the screen or the trackpad or the keyboard because they're all so close together and stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 它搞不清你到底是在摸屏幕、触控板还是键盘，因为它们挨得太近了之类的，对吧？

sentences.en: And it's like, hey, can you like filter out the mistaken touches, right?
sentences.zh: 然后就说，嘿，你们能过滤掉那些误触吗，对吧？

sentences.en: Like if you're swiping the trackpad, you want to ignore the screen.
sentences.zh: 比如你在滑触控板时，你希望忽略屏幕。

sentences.en: You didn't mean to touch the screen.
sentences.zh: 你并不是故意要碰屏幕的。

sentences.en: It was just too close to the trackpad, right?
sentences.zh: 只是离触控板太近了，对吧？

sentences.en: Which, of course, I had told them when they were making the phone that they put the trackpad too close to the screen.
sentences.zh: 当然，我以前做手机的时候就告诉过他们，他们把触控板离屏幕太近了。

sentences.en: But anyhow, it's like fix it in software, right?
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，就是说在软件里修复它，对吧？

sentences.en: So you get these bug reports like that and the bug is called a Mike L bug because it's not someone complaining, it's Mike L complaining that he was scrolling his trackpad and he
sentences.zh: 所以你会收到这种Bug报告，这个Bug被称为迈克·L Bug，因为不是别人在抱怨，而是迈克·L在抱怨他滚动触控板时

sentences.en: got screen input accidentally, right?
sentences.zh: 不小心触发了屏幕输入，对吧？

sentences.en: And so those were like obviously high priority bugs because it's, oh, it's a Mike L bug.
sentences.zh: 所以这些显然是高优先级Bug，因为哦，这是个迈克·L Bug。

sentences.en: You got to fix it right away.
sentences.zh: 你得马上修复它。

sentences.en: And my manager would take that part out of the bug.
sentences.zh: 而我的经理会把Bug里的那部分去掉。

sentences.en: If it said Mike L bug in there, which everyone just knew what that meant, he would just remove it and leave a comment saying, remove superfluous information.
sentences.zh: 如果里面写了迈克·L Bug——大家其实都知道这意味着什么——他就会直接删掉，并留下一条评论说：删除多余信息。

sentences.en: Because my manager was just like, I don't care whose bug it is.
sentences.zh: 因为我的经理就是那种态度，我不在乎是谁的Bug。

sentences.en: It's either important or it's not important.
sentences.zh: 它要么重要，要么不重要。

sentences.en: And we're just like, man, you're just trying to get yourself fired, right?
sentences.zh: 而我们当时就想，天哪，你这是在给自己找解雇信吧，对吧？

sentences.en: But he would do that.
sentences.zh: 但他确实会这么做。

sentences.en: But the other part of that story is that every now and then I would be like, okay, I need to know, was he scrolling up because he touched the trackpad and then the screen or was he
sentences.zh: 但那个故事的另一部分是，每隔一段时间我就会想，好吧，我需要知道，他是因为先摸了触控板然后摸屏幕才往上滚的，还是

sentences.en: like scrolling down?
sentences.zh: 他向下滚？

sentences.en: He touched the screen, then the trackpad because you know, you're going to handle that differently.
sentences.zh: 他是先摸了屏幕，然后摸触控板，因为你知道，你得用不同的方式处理这些情况。

sentences.en: It's easy to say, it's easy when you touch the screen, you can say, well, did you just touch the trackpad like this many microseconds ago?
sentences.zh: 说起来容易，当你摸屏幕时很简单，你可以说，好吧，你是在多少微秒前刚好摸了触控板吗？

sentences.en: Because I'll ignore the screen touch, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我会忽略屏幕触摸，对吧？

sentences.en: But if you go the other way and you touch the screen and then the trackpad, am I going to delay every screen input to say, well, let me wait, let me wait to see if he touched
sentences.zh: 但如果你反过来，先摸屏幕再摸触控板，我是不是要延迟每一个屏幕输入，以便说，好吧，让我等等，让我等等看他有没有摸

sentences.en: the trackpad, right?
sentences.zh: 触控板，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think I ended up actually with, there's a region at the bottom of the screen where I do delay the touch input because it's like, well, wait and see if he touched the trackpad.
sentences.zh: 我想我最后确实搞出了一个方案，屏幕底部有一个区域，我在那里会延迟触摸输入，因为这就相当于，好吧，等等看他有没有摸触控板。

sentences.en: But anyhow, I needed to know which, what, you know, it's like someone go ask Mike L what was going, like, give me more information.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，我需要知道到底是哪种情况，你知道的，就好像有人去问问迈克·L到底怎么回事，呃，给我更多信息。

sentences.en: And the people that, because he's obviously not logging his own bug, right?
sentences.zh: 而那些人——因为他显然不会自己去提Bug，对吧？

sentences.en: Someone else logs the bug for him into the system.
sentences.zh: 是别人帮他把Bug录入系统的。

sentences.en: You ask that person, it's like, I need more information.
sentences.zh: 你去问那个人，就说，我需要更多信息。

sentences.en: They're like, oh yeah, we'll talk to Mike and we'll come back to you.
sentences.zh: 他们就会说，哦，好的，我们会去跟迈克谈谈，然后再回复你。

sentences.en: And they never get back to you because they don't talk to him because they're afraid to because he's the big bad boss, right?
sentences.zh: 结果他们再也没有回复过，因为他们根本不敢跟他谈，由于他是那个位高权重的可怕老板，对吧？

sentences.en: And so finally, one day, you know, every company has their all hands and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以终于有一天，你知道的，每家公司都有全员大会之类的东西。

sentences.en: So I went to one of the all hands, I waited to the end, Mike L does his stalking.
sentences.zh: 于是我参加了一个全员大会，一直等到最后，迈克·L在四处闲逛。

sentences.en: I walked up to him at the end.
sentences.zh: 最后我朝他走了过去。

sentences.en: I said, hey, I got a bug.
sentences.zh: 我说，嘿，我有个Bug。

sentences.en: I need to know, like, tell me, tell me, I need more information.
sentences.zh: 我需要知道，快告诉我，告诉我，我需要更多信息。

sentences.en: He's like, oh yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，行啊。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: Blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 巴拉巴拉。

sentences.en: We talked about this bug for five minutes.
sentences.zh: 我们围绕这个Bug聊了五分钟。

sentences.en: And I told him, I said, look, I've asked for this information.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他，我说，听着，我已经索要过这个信息了。

sentences.en: No one will give it to me.
sentences.zh: 没人肯给我。

sentences.en: And he's like, just come to my office.
sentences.zh: 他说，直接来我办公室就行。

sentences.en: He's like, just come find me.
sentences.zh: 他说，直接来找我。

sentences.en: And I'm like, excellent.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，太棒了。

sentences.en: I am now like firsthand, you know, first name basis with Mike L.
sentences.zh: 我现在可以说跟迈克·L直接建立起第一手的、直呼其名的关系了。

sentences.en: Just, hey, buddy, Mike.
sentences.zh: 就直接，嘿，老兄，迈克。

sentences.en: You know, just walk in when he's got a big meeting with somebody.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当他在跟什么人开大会的时候直接走进去。

sentences.en: Say, Mike, I just got to, everybody, stop for a second.
sentences.zh: 说，迈克，我有个问题，大家，等一下。

sentences.en: I got a quick question for Mike here.
sentences.zh: 我得问迈克一个小问题。

sentences.en: He's my guy, my guy Mike, you know.
sentences.zh: 他是我的哥们，我的好兄弟迈克，你懂的。

sentences.en: I'm important.
sentences.zh: 我很重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then I left the company.
sentences.zh: 然后我就从公司离职了。

sentences.en: So I didn't actually get to use my power, I don't think.
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉自己其实并没用上这种特权。

sentences.en: It was right before I left.
sentences.zh: 那正是在我离开前不久。

sentences.en: And for those of you that are extremely confused on why Tony was talking about a trackpad on a cell phone, I will link a photo of, I'm not sure, I had a BlackBerry Bold.
sentences.zh: 对于你们当中那些对托尼为什么在手机上讨论触控板感到极其困惑的人，我会放一张照片链接，我不确定，我以前用过黑莓Bold。

sentences.en: I think it had one of those trackpads.
sentences.zh: 我想它就带那种触控板。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 你用过黑莓？

sentences.zh: 他是加拿大人。

sentences.en: We give him, every Canadian gets one when they're born.
sentences.zh: 我们送的，每个加拿大人出生时都会发一个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: When you graduate high school, you got one.
sentences.zh: 当你高中毕业时，你就能拿一个。

sentences.en: I had a flip phone or slider phone when I graduated, when I was in high school.
sentences.zh: 我高中毕业时拿的是翻盖手机或滑盖手机。

sentences.en: And then I used that into university.
sentences.zh: 然后我在大学里一直用那个。

sentences.en: But as soon as I had my first co-op at Manulife in Toronto, I thought to myself, well, I'm joining the business world.
sentences.zh: 但当我刚在多伦多的宏利金融（Manulife）开始第一份带薪实习时，我心里想，好吧，我要踏入商业世界了。

sentences.en: I'll be ostracized if I show up without a BlackBerry.
sentences.zh: 如果我没带黑莓手机现身，我会被孤立的。

sentences.en: So I bought a BlackBerry Bold.
sentences.zh: 所以我买了一部黑莓Bold。

sentences.en: Wait, you had an iPhone.
sentences.zh: 等等，你用过iPhone。

sentences.en: I did not have an iPhone.
sentences.zh: 我没用过iPhone。

sentences.en: I had one of those flip phones or slider phones.
sentences.zh: 我用的是那种翻盖或滑盖手机。

sentences.en: The early days.
sentences.zh: 那还是早期。

sentences.en: Anyone who's played NHL video games, NHL 2K, even like 2K14, 2K15, I don't know when it stopped.
sentences.zh: 任何玩过NHL电子游戏的人，比如《NHL 2K》，甚至像2K14、2K15，我不知道是什么时候停的。

sentences.en: But there's like the trading, the general manager mode where you can trade players with other teams and stuff.
sentences.zh: 但里面有那种交易、总经理模式，你可以在那里与其他球队交易球员之类的。

sentences.en: It shows a picture of a BlackBerry phone as like, hey, you're getting a call from Vancouver
sentences.zh: 它会显示一张黑莓手机的照片，意思就像是，嘿，你正接到来自温哥华

sentences.en: Canucks.
sentences.zh: 加人队的电话。

sentences.en: They want to make a trade.
sentences.zh: 他们想做一笔交易。

sentences.en: And it shows a BlackBerry phone.
sentences.zh: 然后画面上显示一部黑莓手机。

sentences.en: And I'm sure BlackBerry paid to get this like advertising built in.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定黑莓花钱把这种广告植入进去了。

sentences.en: But it was also true.
sentences.zh: 但这也是事实。

sentences.en: That was what it would be like to be a manager.
sentences.zh: 当经理差不多就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: Every manager had a BlackBerry.
sentences.zh: 每个经理都有一部黑莓。

sentences.en: There's no doubt.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Every GM in the NHL and every sport was carrying a BlackBerry so that they could do their stuff.
sentences.zh: NHL以及各大体育联盟的每个总经理都随身带着黑莓，好让他们能处理工作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: BBM was like kind of, not really like Messenger, but it was like you could only message people that had BBM, right?
sentences.zh: BBM有点像，其实不太像Messenger，但它的机制是你只能给也有BBM的人发消息，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So like it was this, it was like, you know, I'm not sure if it was before Facebook or whatever, but it was tapping into the whole, you know, same thing with Bloomberg.
sentences.zh: 所以这就有点像，你知道的，我不太确定这是否在Facebook之前什么的，但它利用了那种，你知道的，彭博社也是同一道理。

sentences.en: You know, you can't message people.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你不能随便给别人发消息。

sentences.en: I think that's changed.
sentences.zh: 我想现在这已经变了。

sentences.en: But at one point in time, people on Wall Street, like you were outside of Wall Street if you didn't have a Bloomberg.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时期，华尔街的人，如果你没有彭博终端，你就像是被排除在华尔街之外一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's the same thing.
sentences.zh: 道理是一样的。

sentences.en: It's a critical mass.
sentences.zh: 这就是临界规模。

sentences.en: Everyone's there because everyone's there.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在那儿，因为大家都那儿。

sentences.en: Everyone had BBM.
sentences.zh: 人人都用BBM。

sentences.en: And then.
sentences.zh: 然后呢。

sentences.en: Or like the, you know, the green bubble versus the blue bubble on iMessage.
sentences.zh: 或者就像iMessage上的绿气泡与蓝气泡一样。

sentences.en: You know, are you another trusted iPhone user or are you the other?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你是另一个受信任的iPhone用户，还是说你是异类？

sentences.en: You know, Chandler, if he ever listens to this, is going to like, you know, just tell him now, Chandler, just 10 seconds.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，钱德勒如果以后听到这个，肯定会像——我现在就直接告诉他，钱德勒，给你10秒钟。

sentences.en: You got to cover your ears because I'm going to say the word patent.
sentences.zh: 你得捂住耳朵，因为我要说出“专利”这个词了。

sentences.en: And, but I think BlackBerry has a patent on speech bubbles in like iMessage and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 但是，我认为黑莓在iMessage之类的对话气泡上拥有专利。

sentences.en: Like Gary Klassen, the guy who wrote BBM.
sentences.zh: 就像加里·克拉森（Gary Klassen），那个编写BBM的人。

sentences.en: And so every phone in the world, you know, does speech bubbles.
sentences.zh: 所以世界上每一部手机，你知道的，都用了对话气泡。

sentences.en: And I don't know, you know, it's corporate, you know, patents, right?
sentences.zh: 我不知道，你知道的，这就是企业专利，对吧？

sentences.en: The way, you know, they, no one sues anyone unless everyone sues everybody.
sentences.zh: 那种，你知道的，没人去起诉任何人，除非所有人互相起诉。

sentences.en: And I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 这就是冷战。

sentences.en: So here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 所以情况是这样的。

sentences.en: Back to the patent story.
sentences.zh: 回到专利的故事。

sentences.en: BlackBerry, when I was there, had 40,000 patents, right?
sentences.zh: 黑莓在我还在那儿的时候，拥有40,000项专利，对吧？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: 40,000 mobile, you know, in a good industry patents, right?
sentences.zh: 40,000项移动领域的专利，你知道的，在好行业里的专利，对吧？

sentences.en: And then someone sat down, like, how do you figure out how much that's worth?
sentences.zh: 然后有人坐下来想，你该怎么弄清楚这些到底值多少钱呢？

sentences.en: Do you look at all 40,000 patents?
sentences.zh: 你要把全部40,000项专利都看一遍吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: You take a, you do a sampling, right?
sentences.zh: 你采用抽样，对吧？

sentences.en: You sample some number of patents and you look at them and say, well, this one's worth this much money.
sentences.zh: 你抽样一定数量的专利，查看它们并说，好吧，这一项值这么多钱。

sentences.en: This one's worth this much money.
sentences.zh: 这一项值这么多钱。

sentences.en: You make some kind of guess at how much this patent is worth.
sentences.zh: 你对这项专利到底值多少钱做出某种猜测。

sentences.en: And then you average it out.
sentences.zh: 然后求平均值。

sentences.en: And you say, well, every patent here in this portfolio is worth about $100,000.
sentences.zh: 然后你会说，好吧，这个专利组合里的每一项专利大约值10万美元。

sentences.en: And so the whole patent portfolio is worth $4 billion.
sentences.zh: 所以整个专利组合价值40亿美元。

sentences.en: So like BlackBerry, even if they did nothing else, was worth $4 billion because they're sitting on $4 billion worth of patents, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，即使黑莓什么都不做，它也价值40亿美元，因为它手握价值40亿美元的专利，对吧？

sentences.en: But that also means that if I write another patent, it's worth $100,000.
sentences.zh: 但这也意味着，如果我再写一个专利，它就值10万美元。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter if it's good or bad, right?
sentences.zh: 管它写得好还是坏呢，对吧？

sentences.en: Because as long as it's a patent, it goes into the pool of, well, on average, they're worth
sentences.zh: 因为只要它是一个专利，它就会进入那个资产池，反正平均下来，它们都值
10万美元。

sentences.en: So every patent I wrote is another $100,000 on their books.
sentences.zh: 所以我写的每一项专利，都能在他们的账面上增加10万美元。

sentences.en: So I'm just like, I'll just, how many do you want?
sentences.zh: 所以我就会想，行吧，你们想要多少？

sentences.en: Do you want 10 patents?
sentences.zh: 你们想要10个专利吗？

sentences.en: I'll write 10 patents.
sentences.zh: 我来写10个专利。

sentences.en: I wrote patents for like the watch, right?
sentences.zh: 我连手表之类的东西都写过专利，对吧？

sentences.en: Like when the Apple watch came out, I'm like, how do you, you know, and I won't get into these, it's okay, Chandler, I won't get into these patents.
sentences.zh: 就像苹果手表刚出来的时候，我就在想，你怎么，你知道的，我不想深究这些，没关系，钱德勒，我不会深究这些专利的。

sentences.en: But like, how do you input text on a watch?
sentences.zh: 但是，在手表上怎么输入文字呢？

sentences.en: It would be really hard, right?
sentences.zh: 这真的很难，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's like a small surface.
sentences.zh: 因为它的表面太小了。

sentences.en: But if you really want to input text on a phone, on a watch, I thought up 10 ways of doing it.
